label: Maltose alpha14 linkage model
adaptation_note: Linked molecular connectivity and stereochemical panels. Native ring coordinates and atom codes are schematic; all 24 source heavy-atom connections and their source wedge/plain assignments are retained across the sequence. Hydrogens remain implicit. The bridge and beta reducing-end example are explicit, not a stereochemistry-free graph.
acceptance_requirement: Retain atom connections, linkage positions and the source stereochemical distinctions across the full sequence; connectivity alone is insufficient.

frames.title: Donor ring connectivity
frames.teaching_key: Donor glucopyranose ring, connectivity reference only. Starting at the rightmost carbon and reading clockwise: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, then ring oxygen O5 at upper right. Carbon = single ring, oxygen = double ring. Bond lengths and angles are schematic; these reference panels do not encode stereochemistry. The following named substituent/bridge panels supply every source external bond. The reducing ring is the source beta reducing-end example; it is not a claim that maltose cannot mutarotate.

frames.title: Donor C2–O-H: down

Three widening separated hashes encode below the ring reference plane. This is source bond 6, reoriented horizontally for reading; it is not a new spatial molecular angle. Read alongside the numbered ring reference.

frames.title: Alpha C1–O–C4 glycosidic bridge
frames.teaching_key: Left single circle = donor C1; centre double circle = bridge oxygen; right single circle = reducing-ring C4. Each set of three hashes is the source below-plane bond; hashes widen toward the oxygen from both carbons. Donor C1 below versus its C5–C6 substituent above defines the depicted alpha donor linkage. This joins C1 to C4 through oxygen, not a direct C–C bond. Each ring and all remaining substituents are provided separately. Relative pin distances are schematic.
